english: For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $a_{n}=\dfrac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}e^{k^{3}/n^{4}}$. If $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(a_{n}\right)^{n}=e^{\lambda}$, then the value of $\lambda$ is ______.
hindi: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ के लिए माना कि $a_{n}=\dfrac{1}{n}\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}e^{k^{3}/n^{4}}$ है। यदि $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}\left(a_{n}\right)^{n}=e^{\lambda}$ है, तो $\lambda$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $n(a_{n}-1)$ lies between $\dfrac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n^{2}}$ and $\dfrac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n^{2}}+\dfrac1n$, both $\to\dfrac14$; by sandwich $n(a_{n}-1)\to\dfrac14$
solution_full: The sum has no closed form, so $a_{n}$ is squeezed. Let $t_{k}=\dfrac{k^{3}}{n^{4}}$; for $1\le k\le n$, $0<t_{k}\le\dfrac{n^{3}}{n^{4}}=\dfrac{1}{n}$.

Sum of cubes: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}k^{3}=\dfrac{n^{2}(n+1)^{2}}{4}$, so $\displaystyle\sum t_{k}=\dfrac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n^{2}}$. Also $\displaystyle\sum t_{k}^{2}\le n\cdot\dfrac{1}{n^{2}}=\dfrac{1}{n}$.
Dividing by $n$: $1+\dfrac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n^{3}}\le a_{n}\le1+\dfrac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n^{3}}+\dfrac{1}{n^{2}}$. Both bounds tend to $1$, so $a_{n}\to1$ and $(a_{n})^{n}$ is a $1^{\infty}$ form.
For a $1^{\infty}$ form, $\displaystyle\lim(a_{n})^{n}=e^{\lim n(a_{n}-1)}$. Multiplying the bounds by $n$: $\dfrac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n^{2}}\le n(a_{n}-1)\le\dfrac{(n+1)^{2}}{4n^{2}}+\dfrac{1}{n}$.
Both sides tend to $\dfrac{1}{4}$, so by the sandwich theorem $n(a_{n}-1)\to\dfrac{1}{4}$.
originality_note: New: the base of the 1^infinity form is the average of e^{k^3/n^4}, a sum with no closed form, so its first-order deviation n(a_n - 1) is obtained by squeezing e^t between 1 + t and 1 + t + t^2 and using the sum of cubes (way 5). Closest known: lim prod (1 + k/n^2) = sqrt(e) and averages of e^{k/n^2} (a GP). Different because: the exponent k^3/n^4 blocks the GP closed form and the quadratic error term must be shown negligible.
blueprint_concepts: Evaluation of limit involving exponential and logarithmic functions

concept_use.one raise to infinity form: a_n -> 1 and the exponent is n, so the limit is e^{lim n(a_n - 1)}.
concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving exponentia: The bounds 1 + t <= e^t <= 1 + t + t^2 on [0,1] replace the exponential terms.
concept_use.Sandwich Theorem: n(a_n - 1) is squeezed between (n+1)^2/(4n^2) and (n+1)^2/(4n^2) + 1/n, both tending to 1/4.
